# One walk, two lengths

## Decision and evidence boundary

Propose a representative week, Monday 14 to Sunday 20 September 2026, around choosing the short or long Baldrys circuit at Greens Bush. This is a production and design example, not an accepted publishing calendar. The September 4 PI Insider Picks already covers “Baldry’s Creek Track, Red Hill South”. Use that coverage as the refresh lead, not as independent proof of track conditions.[9] Parks Victoria identifies Baldry's Circuit Walking Trail near Main Ridge, with a 1.6 km short circuit and a 3.6 km long circuit.[12] The concrete decision is which length belongs in the reader's day.

The new service draft supplies the route distinction and practical checks missing from the extracted existing item. Preserve the historical September 4 article and its date. Propose a linked service article rather than silently replacing the whole multi-pick article. A release editor can instead integrate the service text into an appropriate existing evergreen record after confirming its canonical identity. No repository or public page has changed.

All copy below is complete for review. Citation markers and `to verify` notes travel with the manuscript; the design pack must expose them in an evidence drawer and retain visible draft/hold badges. They are not evidence of editorial approval. Research observed September 5 UTC, which falls on September 6 in Melbourne during this work window. Exact site publication/update dates were not supplied by Parks Victoria. Fetch date is not a fact-verification or local-visit date.

Read the four current briefs and both mandatory frozen voice/principles files. The supplied strategy recommends a refresh-first shadow package with an anchor, social preparation and email draft.[5] Its frontmatter still says pending verification; the separate September 6 practice-lead receipt accepts that report within its stated scope.[6] This manuscript has no such receipt yet. The current brief permits official listings for a draft, with local-knowledge gaps marked, and requires independent local evidence at publication.[4]

## Audience and reader value

Primary audience: Peninsula locals and Melbourne day-trippers choosing one outdoor component of a September day. Secondary audience: visitors booking ahead who need a named starting point and a manageable decision. These are brief-led audience hypotheses, not measured segments.[1] Avoid unsupported promises about children, wheelchair access, dogs, trip times or crowd levels.

Reader job: “Help me choose a walk length, understand the trade-off and find the official conditions before I set out.” Value: one comparison, one source of current park advice, no itinerary padded with unverified venues. The editorial judgement is that the short circuit fits a day with another commitment; the long circuit fits a day centred on walking. This is a reasoned proposal based on published distance and route descriptions, not a report of a visit. Mark both judgements for local review.

Business hypothesis, proposed: practical comparison content may earn relevant search visits, saved social posts and useful referrals to official planning information. No conversion or revenue effect is established. No venue pays for selection, and this pack contains no offer, affiliate link or endorsement. Commercial interest cannot change the route judgement. Do not ask a venue to approve PI's opinion.

## Channel strategy and cadence

Website owns durable detail, corrections and source links. Email offers a compact forward-looking plan to existing consenting subscribers, not an article pasted into an inbox. Instagram makes the length choice legible in a few screens and directs readers back to the source-backed guide. Channel configuration, analytics, subscriber consent records and social publishing access remain unverified; the briefs do not establish them as operational.[2][3]

Keep other channels out of this pilot. A separate TikTok, Facebook, paid campaign or partner mailout adds access, moderation and creative work without a tested need. The reel below is a fully scripted substitute for the carousel, not another promised feed post.

## W01: complete web service draft

**Draft date:** 6 September 2026. Public updated/verified label: hold until the release editor records the appropriate review; never substitute this draft date for a completed visit.

### Choose your circuit

Start at Baldry Crossing for a walk through Greens Bush, near Main Ridge. Parks Victoria describes two circuits here: a 1.6 km short loop and a 3.6 km long loop.[12]

For a September day with another commitment, choose the short circuit. Its published route passes through eucalypt forest, with Peppermint, Messmate and Manna Gum among the trees Parks Victoria identifies.[12] The shorter distance is the reason to choose it, rather than a promise about how quickly your group will finish. **[to verify: independent local review of the recommendation and current route suitability]**

Choose the long circuit when the walk is the main part of your September plan. Parks Victoria describes a route further into the forest, with several creek crossings and fern gullies.[12] That gives the longer option a different focus as well as more distance. **[to verify: independent local review of this comparison and current creek-crossing conditions]**

| Choice | Parks Victoria distance | Published route detail | PI planning judgement |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baldrys Short Circuit | 1.6 km | Eucalypt forest | Choose it when walking shares the day with another commitment. Local review pending. |
| Baldrys Long Circuit | 3.6 km | Further into the forest, with creek crossings and fern gullies | Choose it when the walk is your main outing. Local review pending. |

Distances and route details: Parks Victoria.[12]

### Start at Baldry Crossing

Parks Victoria directs both circuits to Baldry Crossing and identifies a picnic area there.[12][13] Bring a snack if you want to make the crossing your pause before or after the walk. **[to verify: current picnic facilities and access before retaining this practical suggestion at release]**

Use the park's own directions to plan your arrival. Walking time, parking capacity, toilet access and public-transport connections need separate checks for your group; this guide gives no estimate for them.

### Before you go

Check the Parks Victoria page when you plan and again before setting out. The page flags uneven ground and slippery surfaces, and advises visitors to check changed conditions and closures.[12] The short circuit's distance alone does not establish step-free access.

For this September planning window, Parks Victoria's notice says fox trapping and baiting in Mornington Peninsula National Park, including Greens Bush, will continue until October 2026. It says short sections of secondary tracks may close for the work.[12] Check the latest notice and follow signs on site. This notice does not establish that either Baldrys circuit is closed or open on your chosen date.

The park prohibits pet dogs. Parks Victoria provides separate entry guidance for assistance dogs.[12] Check that guidance if it applies to your visit.

Parks Victoria also asks visitors to check the Fire Danger Rating and Total Fire Ban information before visiting.[12] Follow its current safety advice, along with any closure directions.

**Primary link:** Check Parks Victoria conditions → CONDITIONS

### Make the length the decision

Keep the 1.6 km circuit for a September plan that leaves room for something else. Give the 3.6 km circuit its own place in the day. Both start at Baldry Crossing; the longer route adds the creek crossings and fern gullies described by Parks Victoria.[12] **[to verify: PI's independent local judgement before publication]**

**Secondary link:** Read the September 4 picks → ARCHIVE

## Measures and production budget

All measures are proposed. There is no retrieved analytics baseline, audience count, click result or delivery record. GA4 and other measurement lanes remain unavailable/unverified under the current brief.[3]

| Surface | Useful signal, if authorised and instrumented | Interpretation and limit |
|---|---|---|
| Web | Unique article sessions; unique outbound CONDITIONS clickers divided by article sessions; internal ARCHIVE clicks | Official-source referrals are a planning-action proxy, not proof of visits or satisfaction |
| Email | Unique GUIDE clickers divided by delivered emails; unsubscribes and complaints | Use delivered, not sent, as denominator. Opens are diagnostic only, not success proof |
| Instagram carousel | Saves/reach; shares/reach; separately attributed guide sessions | Native saves suggest reference value, not completed outings. Reach is not audience intent |
| Stories | Link sticker taps and attributed guide sessions, with frame reach | Tap and arrival are different events; do not call them identical conversions |
| Optional reel | Completion and guide sessions if available | Compare marginal effort and planning referrals, not views alone |
| Trust/workload | Factual corrections, unresolved holds, rights incidents, human minutes and rework | Missing data is N/A, never zero |

Proposed tags, only once link infrastructure is commissioned: `utm_campaign=greens_bush_2026_09`, `utm_source=newsletter` or `instagram`, `utm_medium=email` or `organic_social`, and `utm_content=e01`, `i01`, `i02` or `r01`. Do not append marketing tags to official safety links. Cross-device identities and visits to the park remain unknown. No cross-channel unique total without a defensible deduplication method.

Review production the following Monday, then assess reader signals seven days after each actual authorised release, in Australia/Melbourne time. Record property/account, extraction time, window, event definitions, bot/internal exclusions and denominators. A proposed four-week pilot gives more context than declaring success from one week; no numerical uplift target without a real baseline. Continue if verified planning actions recur and quality/effort remain acceptable. Simplify if the same result takes less work in a static format. Stop promotion for unresolved safety or rights issues, irrespective of engagement.

Proposed weekly envelope: 720 person-minutes (12 hours), an estimate rather than time recorded. Research and conditions checks 120; anchor and dispatch writing 150; email/social adaptation 90; type-led design 150; independent fact/rights review 60; editorial approval plus link/accessibility QA 90; measurement and maintenance preparation 60. This excludes travel, new photography, implementation, account setup, sends and publishing. An independent local call/visit is a release prerequisite but is not claimed to fit this remote-production allowance; separately estimate and commission it. Optional reel must replace, not add to, the feed-design allowance; defer it if it cannot fit. Record actual work and rework at the role level before setting a recurring quota.

Suggested role assignment, not named-staff availability: writer/researcher prepares evidence and copy; designer creates original graphic assets; independent local reviewer verifies practical judgement; editorial/practice lead accepts the revision; Max resolves commissioning within the current gates. A separate authorised executor owns any future release and exact readback. No person or system has accepted those assignments in this manuscript.

| Q01 | James byline follows brief, but this particular text lacks editorial adoption and practice-lead acceptance | All | Show review-only, retain byline approval flag |
| M01 | Measurement setup and baseline absent | All | Report N/A; no invented results |

Check F03 again for the Sunday forward-look, since it frames 26–27 September rather than only the production week. “Until October 2026” preserves the source wording and must not become “ends 31 October”. A generic site notice cannot establish a particular circuit's closure. A successful fetch never advances `last_fact_verified` or `last_editorially_reviewed`.

## Source ledger and verification notes

The numbered ledger is `campaign-source-ledger.json`; the inventory links each asset to its source IDs and hold flags. Public PI extraction confirms existing coverage only, not its factual accuracy. Direct Parks Victoria extraction supports route distances, start point, published descriptions and the named alerts. The programmatic extractor first returned 403s; the direct extraction tool subsequently returned the full official pages. Those failed attempts remain in `campaign-source-extracts.json` and are not cited as successful evidence. Successful excerpts and claim notes live in `campaign-verified-source-notes.json`.

Humanizer pass: removed brochure adjectives, dramatic kickers and invented field texture; kept named places and the decision. Remaining risk is repeated short/long phrasing across derivatives, which is intentional for consistent facts, not extra claims. Editorial copy uses no em-dashes, fabricated quotes, visitor statistics, firsthand visit claims or automated-capability promises. Formal independent review remains outstanding.
